newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Mutiny reported against rebel Afghan leader Dostum.
newsitem.headline: Mutiny reported against rebel Afghan leader Dostum.

text.p: A Pakistan-based news agency on Monday reported a mutiny against northern Afghan leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum in his stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said rebels within Dostum's forces led by General Abdul Malik had begun a revolt in favour of the Islamic Taleban militia, which controls Kabul and more than two-thirds of Afghanistan.

AIP said Malik was a brother of Rasul Pahlivan, a powerful Dostum commander who was assassinated in Mazar-i-Sharif last year. It said details of the reported uprising were sketchy and it was not immediately clear if Dostum had been toppled.

Dostum, an ethnic Uzbek, was a key commander for the pro-communist government led by president Najibullah, who was hanged by the Taleban when they captured Kabul on September 27. He formed a loose alliance with two other leaders after the fall of the capital and their forces have been locked in combat with the Taleban north of Kabul and in northwest Afghanistan.

In April 1992 he switched sides to support mujahideen guerrilla groups which had battled Soviet troops occupying Afghanistan in the 1980s. Dostum's backing enabled the mujahideen to take over Kabul from Najibullah.
In January 1994 he allied with Hezb-i-Islami leader Gulbuddin Hekmatyar to stage an abortive coup attempt in the Afghan capital against then-president Burhanuddin Rabbani.
